problem: Modular object-search pipelines train policies on ground-truth semantics, then zero-shot swap in pretrained (often dated) perception models, using only the latest prediction and no temporal aggregation. Overconfident, uncalibrated probabilities produce many false 'found' decisions and a ~25.8 ppt gap to ground-truth perception.
motivation: The perception gap is often as large as the gap to an optimal policy, yet the literature focuses on policy learning. Because pretrained segmentation models are overconfident and object search is sequential (early errors compound), the paper argues that calibrated probabilities and uncertainty should drive map aggregation and found decisions, without retraining.
key_idea: Use temperature-scaled calibrated segmentation probabilities and their normalized-entropy uncertainty for inverse-uncertainty weighted map aggregation and for an uncertainty-thresholded found decision, plug-in with any pretrained model or policy.
insight: Both calibration and uncertainty-gated found decisions are needed: on EMSANet with the shortest-path policy, plain averaging gets 44.7 SR, calibration alone 44.7, uncertainty-gated found alone 47.9, and both give 73.8 (74.9 with weighting). Latest-prediction mapping collapses to 30.1 SR due to false positives (67% FPR). Relative rankings of aggregation methods stay stable across perception models and policies, and better calibrated models (EMSANet ECE 26%→5%) gain more.
method: Temperature scaling: tune a scalar t on a labeled HM3D image set to scale logits, giving calibrated per-pixel softmax probabilities for any pretrained segmenter (no retraining).
Per-pixel uncertainty: normalized entropy of the calibrated probability vector, in [0,1].

Uncertainty-weighted map aggregation: each 3x3 cm BEV cell holds a class probability vector averaged over N observations with weights 1/u, plus height, occupancy, and map uncertainty (entropy of the aggregated vector); projection uses depth and GT pose.
Map-uncertainty found decision: declare found only if the target is within 1 m and the cell's map uncertainty is below xi=0.4, filtering false positives that vary across views.

Evaluation protocol: a state-independent GT shortest-path policy isolates perception/aggregation effects, plus a PPO RL policy trained with GT semantics and deployed with learned perception; baselines tuned with TPE (20 trials).

setting.backbone: Pretrained segmentation models (EMSANet, Segformer, Mask-RCNN, frozen, temperature-scaled) + RL policy (Schmalstieg et al., PPO trained with GT semantics) or GT shortest-path policy
setting.training_data: No new training; only one scalar temperature tuned on a labeled HM3D image set; RL policy trained with ground-truth semantics; perception models pretrained on ADE20k / SUN RGB-D+Hypersim / COCO
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, pitch -20°) with localization (GT pose)
setting.action_space: continuous velocity actions (max linear 0.25 m/s) with a Stop/found decision
setting.privileged: GT pose/localization; GT semantics used for RL policy training; GT shortest-path navmesh in the shortest-path evaluation

numbers.eval_set_note: Habitat 2023 ObjectNav validation split, modified (plant class omitted, landscape camera, continuous actions); shortest-path policy
numbers.extra: GT shortest-path policy, not a learned policy; metrics over full trajectory

numbers.eval_set_note: Habitat 2023 ObjectNav val split with modifications; RL policy
numbers.backbone: EMSANet + RL policy trained with GT semantics
numbers.extra: policy trained with GT perception, deployed with learned perception; GT perception reference SR 75.0

numbers_note: Mask-RCNN only has baselines (Latest, Hits/Views, Skill Fusion), not the proposed method. The paper's ObjectNav setup is modified so not directly comparable to the official leaderboard.
results: With EMSANet, weighted uncertainty averaging lifts SR from 15.8 (latest) to 56.4 with the RL policy and from 30.1 to 74.9 with the shortest-path policy, beating Skill Fusion (48.4 / 67.8) and Stubborn. It narrows the gap to GT perception (75.0 RL SR) and matches or beats baselines across models, except Skill Fusion with Segformer under RL (54.3 vs 52.9 SR).
limitations: Policy is trained with GT perception and remains unaware of uncertainty; the uncertainty maps are not fed to the policy (left as future work)
Evaluated only on ObjectNav in Habitat/HM3D with GT pose, simulation only; Mask-RCNN can't use the probabilistic aggregation
Thresholds and temperature need tuning, and gains are smaller for poorly calibrated models like Segformer
builds_on: Schmalstieg et al. RL object search
